item.title: Ralliston's Journey through all of the 001 proposals - Part Eight - not_a_seagull's Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Review: Seagull, you clever bastard. I love this one. Whilst I really dislike the in-universe idea that most of the reports are fabricated, I can look past that due to the wonderful rest. I'm not entirely sure this fits the 001 slot, but I don't care. I would want to explain my vote more in-depth… but I genuinely can't for the love of me explain my absolute love for this one. I just sorta adore it to bits. Absolutely wonderful work.

Result: An enthusiastic +1

item.title: Is this...
item.content:encoded:
Is this SCP 001 Azathoth? Are… We the beings whose sole purpose is to keep it in endless slumber, lest creation itself end?!

And, to a lesser note, was the Pulp era an attempt to cultivate a stable of quality (or at least acceptable) authors capable of maintaining a high output of work to keep it entertained?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
+ While there are definitely parallels ...
- While there are definitely parallels ...

001 is less of a stand-in for the authorship than a commentary on the readership. The core idea here is that the entire Foundation universe is in the imagination of a comatose male. If you note the vocalizations in Daevish, it sounds like parents or loved ones who want the subject to wake up and become lucid.

Of course, the Foundation can't let this happen. Why?

Description: SCP-001 is an ongoing ZK-Class "Reality Failure" Scenario.

What was the theme for this day of JamCon again? "It was all a dream."

If he wakes up, the dream ends, and with it, their entire universe.

So they keep him entertained, giving him stories about anomalies and interactions and GoIs to maintain his interest and keep him comatose.

It also serves the purposes 001s are expected to provide well. It explains the origin and nature of their universe, and with it, the nature of the anomalous. Of course, it also comments on the wiki itself, with the first entry they read to him implied to be 173, along with the expansion of the 001 slot and creation of "series".

So while Swann's 001 explains the SCPverse through the perspective of the writers, seagull's 001 explains it through the perspective of the readers, with one particular reader acting as both a framing device and clever in-universe origin story.

There's also the title. "The Sky Above the Port" both fits the general 001 scheme of titles being "The [Thing]", as well as referring to the quote from which TSATPWTCOTTTADC gets their name. (and even makes an appearance in the work!) The title is meant to evoke that whole feeling of being in an artificial world, where you have to fight for your very existence.

This is just so well-done, on many levels. The fact that it was done with a very clever format screw that necessitated complex HTML and done in the JamCon timeframe was just amazing.

Truly a deserving 001 proposal. +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For me, the imagery of the Description wasn't strong enough to engage my interest, meaning that the revelation of the nature of the 001 left me cold. I think part of that is the lack of threat provided - it's never really brought home how dangerous 001 is, to justify the level of containment required. The in-universe side of this also made little sense to me - the idea that the Foundation has to change their database, as opposed to creating a separate set of files to do the story-telling, felt somewhat arbitrary (especially when compared to the previous literature which worked for the anomaly - there didn't seem to be a coherent throughline there). If you really wanted to have the anomaly for some reason require the Foundation's main database to be changed to its whim, why not explore the potential effects of those changes a bit more - how does that impact Foundation operations?

Finally, one nitpick. The notes of the Society for the Containment of the Babel Demon refer to it expressly as SCP-001-2 - was the Foundation not surprised by this use of their nomenclature when they were given the notes?!

I think D is the most likely. The JavaScript here runs on the client side, and your browser will most likely run out of RAM by… uh…

item.title: I dreamed of this 001 proposal
item.content:encoded: Problem is, what I dreamt was also influeced by JorgeLuis Borge's The Library of Babel. More specifically, a passage describing a book comprised of only MCV repeated from beggining to end on the pages of the book and the theories of the librarians that, as the book goes, each MCV affected the next, changing its value. Basically, both things metastasized in my dream and I currently find the real version lackluster. Yup, it's a very dumb reason, but even after reading, I felt the recursive nature of the skip was already lacking. I don't know what else to say.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I wish there was more setup to the recursive nature of the document; you had an opportunity to link this to the trope of a dream about waking up from a dream (about waking up from a dream about waking up from a…). I also feel like you could have been a bit more dream-like with the idea itself (and I agree with others that the intro text is annoying).

That being said, this is a pretty cool idea. The screw actually caught me off-guard, which is pretty rare; it's also an idea that only works as an 001. I feel like this could have been stronger, but what's here is still excellent enough to secure an upvote from me.

Otherwise, this is very good, it's what I like to see in SCPs in that it tells a story that couldn't be told in any other format (normally I hate gimmicky format screws but this is elegant, simple and doesn't interfere with reading). Being able to successfully put together a format screw 001 of this caliber in 24-48 hours is a little scary. Easy +1.
